articles.title: Sky Brown: GB skateboarder wins silver at World Skate Games
articles.summary: Great Britain's youngest Olympic medal winner, Sky Brown, wins silver at the World Skate Games in Paraguay, helping her LA 2028 qualifying hopes.
articles.body:
Great Britain's Sky Brown won silver at the World Skate Games as she continued her bid to qualify for a third Olympic Games.

The 18-year-old skateboarder scored 89.50 points in the women's park final and narrowly missed out on gold to Japan's Mizuho Hasegawa, who scored 91.00.

The competition in Asuncion, Paraguay, was the second event where skaters could earn world skate ranking (WSR) points towards qualifying for Los Angeles 2028, which will be the third Olympic Games to host skateboarding.

In the Tokyo Olympic Games, held in 2021, Brown won bronze to become Great Britain's youngest Olympic medal winner at 13 years old.

Four years later, she added a second bronze at the Paris Olympics.

Brown is also a two-time park world champion, winning titles in 2023 and 2025.

Her 15-year-old brother, Ocean Brown, also competed for Great Britain in Paraguay, in his first appearance at the World Skate Games, but missed out on advancing past the heats.

articles.title: 'India-Pakistan flavour will be missed': Suraj Karkera on rivals' withdrawal from Asian Champions Trophy
articles.summary: The absence of an India-Pakistan clash may take away some of the intensity and excitement from the upcoming Asian Champions Trophy (ACT) Punjab 2026, but
articles.body: The absence of an India-Pakistan clash may take away some of the intensity and excitement from the upcoming Asian Champions Trophy (ACT) Punjab 2026, but defending champions India remain focused on retaining their title, goalkeeper Suraj Karkera has said. With Pakistan withdrawing from the continental tournament and Bangladesh stepping in as their replacement, the Indian team will turn its attention towards continuing its dominance in Asian hockey.Pakistan's withdrawal leaves India-Pakistan rivalry on the sidelinesPakistan's withdrawal has ruled out a potential India-Pakistan showdown at the Asian Champions Trophy, scheduled to be held from October 27 to November 5 across Jalandhar and Mohali in Punjab.Bangladesh have replaced Pakistan in the six-team tournament after the Pakistan Hockey Federation's participation remained subject to government clearance. PHF president Mohyuddin Ahmed Wani had earlier indicated that the federation would follow the government's decision regarding the team's proposed visit to India.India and Pakistan share one of the most intense rivalries in international hockey, with their encounters traditionally drawing considerable attention from fans. However, the recent head-to-head record has heavily favoured India.In their last 20 meetings since 2016, India have won 18 matches, while the remaining two ended in draws. Pakistan are yet to register a victory during that period. Their most recent encounter came in the semifinal of the 2026 Asian Games, where India edged Pakistan 4-3.'India-Pakistan flavour will be missed' - KarkeraKarkera acknowledged that fans would miss the fierce rivalry between the two neighbours, but stressed that players have little control over decisions surrounding participation in international tournaments. The Indian team, he added, would concentrate on performing to the best of its ability.“They are a good team, and athletes never want to pull out of a tournament, but these are things beyond our control. We're just there to go and perform to the best of our ability, and I think the result will take care of itself. The India-Pakistan flavour will be missed by the people, but it is something that is way beyond our say,” Karkera told ANI.The Indian goalkeeper was speaking on the sidelines of a felicitation ceremony where Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth interacted with and felicitated Indian Army sportspersons who participated in the 2026 Asian Games.India aim to defend Asian Champions Trophy titleWith Pakistan out of the tournament, the competition will feature India, Malaysia, Japan, South Korea, China and Bangladesh. India will enter as defending champions, reigning Asian Games gold medallists and the highest-ranked team in the field.The Indian men's hockey team arrives in Punjab on the back of another successful Asian Games campaign in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, where it successfully defended its gold medal with a commanding 5-1 victory over Malaysia in the final.The triumph marked India's fifth men's hockey gold at the Asian Games, following their victories in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022. It also marked a historic edition for Indian hockey, as both the men's and women's teams won gold medals at the same Asian Games for the first time.India, five-time winners of the Asian Champions Trophy, will now look to carry that momentum into the continental competition and strengthen their position among Asia's leading hockey nations.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
